subject: Post-call: Long-window model fit summary + action plan
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Jane Liu <jane.liu@acuityanalytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Long-window model fit summary + action plan

Hi Jane — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps while it's fresh: 

Summary of requirements (from call)
- Primary use case: multi-hour clinical note ingestion and summarization for provider review (~10k–50k token windows per patient).
- Key success metrics: summary fidelity (recall of critical items), truncation avoidance, <750ms median generation latency at 99th percentile for short follow-ups, and predictable token-cost per patient.
- Data constraints: notes contain structured sections (Rx, labs), PHI allowed under BAAs; customer prefers on-dedicated or private deployment for audit controls.

Initial model fit recommendations
- Candidate 1: LlamaX-70B-q4f (recommended for long-window summarization with prefix KV caching enabled) — best balance of fidelity and cost for transcript-heavy inputs.
- Candidate 2: Redwood-Long-13B (quantized, optimized attention) — lower cost; suitable for pilot with aggressive caching & selective summarization.
- Fallback: LlamaX-7B for extreme cost-constrained paths.

Benchmarks & artifacts attached
- Attached: longwindow-bench-summary-20260218.pdf (pilot run on 1k de-identified patient notes). Highlights: LlamaX-70B retained 92% of critical items on our recall eval; Redwood-Long-13B at 85% with 40% cost savings.
- Promptset attached: acq_longwindow_promptset_v1.csv (includes canonical prompts, temperature, and stop-token rules we used).
- Internal note: redwood_model_recommendations.md contains tuning knobs we suggest (KV cache TTLs, batching windows).

Immediate suggested next steps
1) Action: I can provision a short pilot (2–3 days) against a small de-id dataset you provide — aim: validate truncation behavior and summary fidelity.
2) Security: If you confirm the preferred deployment model (Dedicated vs Private), I’ll send the provisioning checklist and security matrix.
3) KPIs: We propose the initial success criteria: >90% critical-item recall (measured on 200 cases), truncation events <3% for >20k token windows.

Would you like us to run the pilot against the LlamaX-70B baseline plus Redwood-Long-13B as a cost-control arm? If yes, I'll open the pilot ticket and share a HubSpot/Drive bundle.

Best,
Jonas
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment stubs: acq_longwindow_promptset_v1.csv (CSV, 42 rows), longwindow-bench-summary-20260218.pdf (6 pages), redwood_model_recommendations.md (markdown, 2 pages)

2) On the fidelity metric — what was the eval rubric and who labeled the "critical items"? Can we see a small sample?
3) Security: we prefer Dedicated for initial pilots; will you be able to provide SOC2 evidence and a brief on key management?

If those look ok, yes — run both models. We'll prepare a de-id sample (~200 patients) and a brief data-extraction script for you.

—Jane

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 20:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: Long-window model fit summary + action plan

Jonas — notes below and attaching the rubric snippet to send to Acuity. Rishi: flag anything I should not share externally.

Rubric sample (paste):
- Case ID 1001: Critical items = {admission reason, abnormal lab flag, med change} — label recall = 3/3
- Case ID 1023: Critical items = {allergies, critical lab > threshold} — label recall = 1/2 (missed lab)
- Labeling: performed by our clinical annotation partner (MedLabel Co.), two-pass adjudication; samples are de-identified before labeling.

On LlamaX-70B behavior: 
- Attention strategy: uses chunked attention with KV sharding plus prefix KV caching; our runtime avoids full quadratic by chunking into 8k windows with streamed recomposition for outputs beyond that.
- Memory: expect ~120 GB GPU RAM for a single 50k token forward pass in peak config; with streaming we operate within 48–64 GB by offloading cache and using truncated recomposition — this is in the tech note (redwood_model_recommendations.md).

Security/SOC2/KMS (Rishi to confirm):
- We can share SOC2 Type II summary and a Dedicated pilot KMS integration checklist. KV cache persistence for Dedicated is configurable and we can set a TTL or never-persist option; audit logs are available per-request for 90 days on Dedicated.

Suggested reply to Jane: attach rubric snippet, SOC2 summary, and a short note on memory/attention (non-confidential tech blurbs). Offer to run parallel pilot on LlamaX-70B + Redwood-Long-13B after they push de-id samples.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
